Capability lookup rule: read current status, lifecycle, canonical route and MCP classification from the canonical source at task start; do not copy a live status snapshot into this file.
Duplicate-build prohibition: do not start from historical roadmap text; resolve the exact capability or alias, inspect its implementation and test evidence, and prefer reuse or migration.
Roadmap authority: reports/SAEE_CAPABILITY_ASSESSMENT_REPORT.md#recommended-next-prs; agent-index.json recommended_next_pr fields are deprecated compatibility metadata.
Ledger sync rule: capability facts update the canonical source and machine projection; update AGENTS.md or this block only when pointers or working rules change, never by copying live capability status.

Governance authority rule: governance/registry/capability-crosswalk.json maps constitutional concepts to existing implementation and is not a second capability fact source; do not copy live status into this file.

The expanded retrieval list below is historical/detail context.

> SAEE is an AI agent long-term stability evaluation and decision infrastructure system. SAEE preserves Silicon-Amplified Evolutionary Ecology as the theory identity and Digital Biosphere Evolution Engine as the engineering core.

External canonical status: `external_canonical_sync_github_pages_release_zenodo_published_profile_social_pending`.

Canonical source: `docs/canonical/SAEE_CANONICAL_METADATA.yaml`.

Do not treat this repository as production-ready, customer-validated, externally validated, a public SDK release, an audit-first SDK, a generic multi-agent framework, a tracing tool, a prompt debugger, or a production monitoring dashboard.

The controlled preview request is a strict, file-backed onboarding envelope. It
requires explicit tenant and experiment scope, rejects secrets/customer records
and external execution fields, and never closes the 24 production blockers.

The Qianfan policy snapshot records official agreement locations and observed
clauses. Retention terms, DPA completion, privacy/legal approval, and production
provider approval remain false until an authorized review supplies evidence.

Digital Biosphere Evolution Engine implements SAEE: Silicon-Amplified Evolutionary Ecology（硅基放大演化生态）.

This repository is the mainline for an evolution-first digital biosphere engine. It is not an AI audit SDK, not a generic multi-agent framework, not a biological imitation, and not a market intelligence tool.

Core loop:
Global Sensing -> Trait Extraction -> Ecological World Model -> Counterfactual Simulation -> Genome Branching -> Controlled Mutation / Recombination -> Sandbox Development -> Pareto Fitness Evaluation -> Selection / Dormancy / Rollback -> Evolutionary Archive -> Next Generation.

Important files:

Safety boundary:
Extract traits, not code. Never execute unknown external repositories, never auto-expand permissions, never copy external code as genome, never auto-publish, and never auto-contact real customers.

Local kernel boundary:
SAEE Kernel v0.1 is a mock-sensing local runnable loop only. It does not claim real external ecological signal ingestion, production deployment, release, DOI, package upload, customer contact, or full evolutionary system completion.

Local v0.2 boundary:
SAEE Kernel v0.2 is an abstract local evolutionary ecology runtime. It keeps multiple genomes, dynamic fitness, selection pressure, and graph lineage, but does not call real APIs, execute external repositories, publish artifacts, or claim production deployment.

Local v0.3 boundary:
SAEE v0.3 is a guarded local meta-evolution bootstrap. It allows rule-genome mutation only inside drift-guarded thresholds and weights; it does not perform unbounded self-modification, real API ingestion, external code execution, publication, or production deployment.

Local v0.4 boundary:
SAEE v0.4 is a local phase-transition evolution-space bootstrap. It mutates dimensions, fitness geometry, selection topology, mutation operator modes, and ecological regimes inside a reproducible simulation only; it does not perform real API ingestion, external code execution, production deployment, or true open-ended evolution.

Local v0.5 boundary:
SAEE v0.5 is a local open-ended evolution physics prototype. It generates laws, fitness functions, selection mechanisms, dimensions, and regimes from local observation signatures only; it does not perform real API ingestion, external code execution, production deployment, or externally verified true open-ended evolution.

Local v0.6 boundary:
SAEE v0.6 is a local evolution observability prototype. It explains v0.5 generated physics through rule genesis, fitness interpretation, semantic lineage, causal reconstruction, self-description, and observer feedback; it does not change v0.5 mechanics or claim externally verified scientific explanation.

Local v0.7 boundary:
SAEE v0.7 is a local reflexive evolution prototype. It makes explanation feedback influence mutation, epistemic fitness, semantic selection, self-model updates, and interpretation-influenced lineage; it does not claim self-awareness, production cognition, or externally verified semantic causality.

Local v0.8 boundary:
SAEE v0.8 is a local identity-stable reflexive evolution prototype. It bounds v0.7 feedback, self-model recursion, selection, and lineage with an identity kernel; it does not claim self-awareness, production cognition, externally verified identity continuity, or externally verified semantic causality.

Phase II boundary:
SAEE Phase II is a local behavior science layer. It observes local run records and extracts behavior patterns, attractors, regimes, topology, drift, invariants, and empirical laws; it does not modify evolution kernels, add mutation or selection mechanics, claim universal laws, or claim external scientific validation.

v1.0 boundary:
SAEE v1.0 is the local stable evolutionary runtime. It keeps one loop, one population pool, one unified fitness function, one selection pass, and one lineage DAG; v0.6-v0.8 and Phase II systems are side-layer references, not runtime dependencies.

v1.0 experiment boundary:
SAEE long-horizon experiments are local-only and observation-only. They run immutable v1.0 through `saee_v1_0.runtime.saee_runtime`, write trace and report files, and do not import v1.0 kernel internals, modify evolution logic, add mechanics, or feed analysis back into runtime.

v1.2 boundary:
SAEE v1.2 is a local empirical alignment layer. It instantiates the formal tuple into a measurable simulation and compares against local GA, ES, and ALife-like baselines; it does not modify v1.1 formal theory, introduce new axioms, call real APIs, execute external repositories, claim universal laws, or claim external scientific validation.

SAEE v1.2 parasitic phase experiment is a local synthetic multi-agent ecology that computes `phi` from resource concentration, normalized reward drift, and lineage dominance, then compares no, weak, and strong governance. It writes local JSONL/CSV/SVG outputs only and does not claim production governance, external validation, or a universal law.

GSP boundary:
SAEE Global State Protocol is a local canonical state surface. It synchronizes theory, engineering, experiment, lineage, and identity into one state object; it does not modify theory, runtime, experiments, or external claims.

Science Lock boundary:
SAEE Science Lock defines SAEE as Computational Evolution Dynamics. It permits describing phenomena, classifying regimes, mapping attractors, and extracting candidate invariants; it forbids treating the next step as a new kernel, new runtime layer, external validation, or universal-law claim.

Phase Diagram v1.0 boundary:
SAEE Phase Diagram v1.0 is existing-log compression only. Its only observed regime transition is stable_regime -> stable_regime with local_observation confidence. Unobserved cross-regime transitions are not empirical facts.

Universal Law Extraction v1.0 boundary:
SAEE law extraction records falsifiable candidate laws from existing phase-space artifacts only. It does not generate new data, modify runtime, or claim universal/external validated laws.

Scientific Closure boundary:
SAEE Scientific Closure records the local evidence chain as an Empirical Computational Evolution Theory Base. It is paper-facing and local only; it does not claim external validation, publication, release, DOI, submission, or universal laws.

Computational Evolution Universality Theory boundary:
Phase IV universality work is hypothesis-only. REDS-MO is a candidate universality class, not a validated universal theory. This stage does not permit kernel evolution, runtime design, mechanism engineering, or new experiment generation without a separate evidence protocol.

Strategic Release boundary:
Layered release files are local preparation artifacts only. Zenodo content is concept/results only. GitHub content is toy abstraction only. The private core remains isolated. No upload, release, tag, push, DOI, publication, submission, or external validation is claimed.

Zenodo Academic Final Package boundary:
`zenodo_release_final/` is definition publishing preparation only. It must contain no executable code, runtime logic, kernel structure, private architecture details, or mutation/selection/fitness/lineage/reproduction implementation. `ZENODO_METADATA.json` is a local draft; no upload or DOI is claimed.

Final Publication Orchestrator boundary:
`zenodo_final_submission/`, `paper_submission/`, `github_public_release/`, and `final_release/` are local publication-preparation artifacts only. They do not modify SAEE, generate new data, submit a paper, upload to Zenodo, create a GitHub release, assign a DOI, push, tag, publish, or disclose kernel/runtime/fitness/selection/mutation/lineage/reproduction implementation.

Phase A / Phase B boundary:
`phase_a_academic/` must be treated as academic definition lock preparation only. `phase_b_product/` must be treated as product abstraction preparation only. A must precede B conceptually. Neither package modifies SAEE, launches a product, publishes science, uploads to Zenodo, submits a paper, releases an SDK, or discloses private kernel/runtime/fitness/selection/mutation/lineage/reproduction implementation.

Commercial Lock boundary:
SAEE's revised commercial identity is competition-testing and stability evaluation for AI agents and decision policies. The primary wedge is AI agent evaluation and policy stress testing, the second wedge is enterprise decision-policy simulation, and quant strategy testing is later only. This is an internal commercial strategy record, not a product launch, customer contact, public SDK release, private-cloud readiness claim, or implementation disclosure.

MVP Product Design boundary:
SAEE MVP is defined as an AI Agent / Strategy Long-term Stability Evaluation Platform. The minimum loop is Upload Agents -> Run Competition -> Simulate Long Horizon -> Compute Stability -> Output Report. The MVP docs define product, UX, engineering, and packaging scope only; they do not implement UI, API, backend, public SDK, production service, customer contact, or private-core disclosure.

MVP API Contract v1.0 boundary:
SAEE API is defined as a black-box long-term competition evaluator for AI systems. It exposes ScenarioBatchRequest, EvaluationRunSummary, StabilityReport, FailureModeReport, SurvivalCurve, and ComparisonRanking only. It records API design, JSON schema, and a local runnable API shell; it does not release a public SDK, launch a product, deploy production service, connect private core, or disclose private kernel/evolution/scoring/selection/mutation/lineage/runtime internals.

MVP FastAPI Backend Skeleton boundary:
SAEE MVP FastAPI Backend is a local runnable API shell under saee_backend/. It implements report-layer create/run/read routes, Pydantic models, deterministic public-shell evaluation, and in-memory storage for product-interface development. It is not production deployment, public SDK release, customer contact, private-core export, private-core integration, kernel modification, runtime modification, or implementation disclosure. The current environment records fastapi_dependency_installed_in_current_environment: false.

MVP Real Evaluation Engine boundary:
SAEE MVP Real Evaluation Engine replaces one-pass shell scoring with deterministic repeat-run evaluation. It computes public MVP stability, survival, failure-rate, collapse, drift, and ranking metrics, then stores runs and metric records in memory. It does not add architecture, theory, new SAEE kernel behavior, external dependencies, database persistence, private production evaluator integration, production deployment, public SDK release, or private implementation disclosure.

Execution Loop v0.1 boundary:
SAEE Execution Loop v0.1 is a local public-shell decision engine inside `saee_backend/`. It runs Input -> Simulation -> Competition -> Scoring -> Decision, enriches `EvaluationRunSummary` with `decision_result`, `recommended_agent`, and `confidence_score`, and does not modify API contract documents or JSON schema. It does not call external APIs, train models, connect private core, deploy production service, release a public SDK, or disclose private implementation.

MVP Landing Page boundary:
`phase_b_product/landing/` is a local static product page for SAEE as an AI Agent / Strategy Long-term Stability Evaluation Platform. It references separate local assets and includes `commercial-readiness.html` as a local browser-readable hold-state page for commercial review. It must not embed base64 image payloads or disclose private kernel/runtime/scoring/selection/mutation/lineage internals. It is not a product launch, production deployment, public SDK release, customer contact, customer validation claim, production readiness claim, or private-core export.

Sites Commercial Evaluation Surface boundary:
`sites/saee-commercial/` is the deployable Sites layer of the same landing surface. It explains SAEE's long-horizon evaluation method and may be deployed privately for product discovery. The site collects no customer data, accepts no payment, executes no external system, and discloses no private kernel. A successful private website deployment is not SAEE product launch, customer validation, production readiness, or permission to contact customers. Current source truth remains `commercial_status=hold`, `production_ready=false`, `customer_validated=false`, and `production_blocker_count=24`.
Historical v4 deployment record: the former `/outreach` and `/validation` routes were owner-operated human workbenches. They are retired from the preferred surface and removed from v5 source. Current canonical agent routing is `agent-interface/agent-manifest.json` and `/for-agents`; v5 deployment status is recorded in `agent-index.json`.

Landing API Integration boundary:
`phase_b_product/landing/app.js` is a local demo bridge from the static landing page to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/experiment/run`. It posts a fixed mock request, renders `decision_result`, `recommended_agent`, `confidence_score`, ranking, and failure summary in page, and relies on local CORS in `saee_backend/main.py`. It does not change API contract documents or JSON schema, enable user uploads, call external APIs, deploy production service, release a public SDK, connect private core, or disclose private implementation.

First User Test Plan boundary:

It does not contact customers, claim customer validation, enable user uploads, launch a product, deploy production service, release a public SDK, modify the landing/API/decision engine, or disclose private implementation.

not claim external validation, production readiness, customer validation, or
public SDK availability.

test with 3 simulated assistant roles and 2 simulated context modes. It is
internal self-play validation only. It does not test external AI assistants,
claim external validation, validate customers, mark production readiness, launch
product, call external APIs, modify backend/runtime/kernel/API schema, or
expose private implementation. Manual external AI assistant testing is deferred
unless explicitly reopened by human decision.

Commercial Boundary Hardening v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/COMMERCIAL_BOUNDARY_V0_1.md` records the
local pre-commercial API shell hardening layer. It adds configurable CORS
origins, optional `X-SAEE-API-Key` guarding for experiment routes, optional
`X-SAEE-Tenant-ID` request-boundary guarding, request limits, optional SQLite
persistence, optional request metadata audit, commercial preflight, and
`GET /ready` boundary reporting, plus controlled-preview support and security
intake contact readiness. It
does not claim production readiness, customer validation, product launch,
public SDK release, private-core connection, production quota readiness,
production database readiness, tenant-isolated storage, tenant billing
isolation, production monitoring readiness, compliance logging readiness, full
vulnerability management, production vulnerability management readiness, or
private-core exposure.

Auth Readiness v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/AUTH_READINESS_V0_1.md` records local
demo auth, controlled-preview API key auth, and missing production identity
infrastructure as separate states. It does not implement or claim OAuth/OIDC,
SSO, RBAC, account provisioning, production authorization, customer validation,
product launch, or production readiness.

Identity Provider Configuration Readiness v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/IDENTITY_PROVIDER_READINESS_V0_1.md`
records local OIDC issuer/audience/JWKS URL and RBAC policy path configuration
readiness for future production-auth implementation review. It does not
contact an identity provider, fetch JWKS, validate tokens, enforce RBAC, close
auth blockers, claim customer validation, launch product, or mark production
auth ready.

RBAC Role-Permission Consistency v0.1 boundary:
The strict local validator rejects route-listed roles that lack the declared
permission, unknown or duplicate roles, duplicate routes, wildcards, and
positive production claims. It reads only local JSON and keeps production auth
and all three auth blockers open.

Tenant-Required Storage Guard v0.1 boundary:
When `SAEE_REQUIRE_TENANT_ID=true`, factory-created memory and SQLite stores
deny unscoped create/save/exists/get/get_runs/get_metrics/list operations. The
application runtime uses the factory; the unused default global store is removed.
Default local mode stays
compatible. This is controlled-preview defense in depth, not production tenant
authorization, production migration, or blocker closure.

Storage Tenant Membership Enforcement v0.1:
Factory-created strict stores snapshot `SAEE_ALLOWED_TENANT_IDS`, fail closed
for empty or invalid configuration, and reject format-valid unlisted tenants
across all seven storage operations. This is configured preview membership,
not identity authentication, full tenant authorization, or production RLS.

Request Limits v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/REQUEST_LIMITS_V0_1.md` records
configurable public-shell limits for agents, repeat runs, time horizon, and
payload bytes before requests enter the evaluation service. It preserves
`api_schema_modified=false`, `runtime_modified=false`,
`kernel_modified=false`, `private_core_exposed=false`, and
`production_ready=false`.

Persistence v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/PERSISTENCE_V0_1.md` records an optional
SQLite-backed public-shell store for completed MVP experiment reports.
`SAEE_STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite` enables local durable persistence, while default
`memory` mode preserves simple local demo behavior. This is not production
database readiness, tenant isolation, backup/restore policy, customer data
governance, or product launch.

Request Audit v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/REQUEST_AUDIT_V0_1.md` records an optional
local JSONL request metadata audit for the public API shell. It records request
ID, method, path, status code, duration, and safe tenant-boundary audit
metadata. Tenant IDs are represented only by SHA-256 hash metadata when
available; raw tenant IDs are not recorded. It does not record request bodies,
response bodies, credentials, API keys, cookies, Authorization headers,
private-core internals, customer secrets, or external assistant output. This is
not tenant audit ownership, production monitoring, compliance logging, SIEM
integration, incident response, customer validation, or product launch.

Operations Telemetry v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/OPERATIONS_TELEMETRY_V0_1.md` records a
local aggregate telemetry snapshot over request audit JSONL metadata. It counts
events, methods, paths, status codes, errors, local duration statistics, and
aggregate tenant-boundary audit metadata counts. It does not inspect bodies,
credentials, raw tenant IDs, private core, or external assistant output, and it
does not export to any external monitoring provider. It is not production
monitoring, alerting, incident response, SLA, support, customer validation, or
product launch.

Operations Telemetry API v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/OPERATIONS_TELEMETRY_API_V0_1.md` records
read-only `GET /operations/telemetry` and `GET /operations/alerts` routes over
the existing local aggregate telemetry and alert-candidate services. It does
not inspect bodies, credentials, private core, or external assistant output,
and it does not export metrics or deliver external alerts. It is not production
monitoring, alerting, incident response, SLA, support, customer validation, or
product launch.

Preview Readiness API v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/PREVIEW_READINESS_API_V0_1.md` records
read-only `GET /readiness/support` and `GET /readiness/vulnerability` routes
over existing support and vulnerability readiness services. It reports boolean
preview-readiness states and does not expose support contact values, security
contact values, credentials, request bodies, or private-core internals. It is
not production support, vulnerability management, SLA, on-call, customer
validation, product launch, or production readiness.

Commercial Preflight v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/COMMERCIAL_PREFLIGHT_V0_1.md` records a
deterministic local configuration preflight for the public API shell. Default
local configuration returns hold; incomplete non-local configuration returns
hold; controlled preview configuration can pass when API key, explicit CORS,
SQLite persistence, request audit, and retention days are enabled. A pass is
controlled-preview configuration only, not production readiness, customer
validation, product launch, public SDK release, external validation, or
private-core exposure.

Data Retention v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/DATA_RETENTION_V0_1.md` records a
default-dry-run local retention utility for public-shell SQLite experiment rows
and request audit JSONL metadata. It does not inspect request bodies, response
bodies, credentials, private-core internals, runtime internals, or customer
secrets. Applying deletion requires both `--apply` and
`SAEE_RETENTION_DRY_RUN=false`. This is not tenant-aware production data
governance, production database readiness, customer validation, or product
launch.

Data Backup v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/DATA_BACKUP_V0_1.md` records a
manual-only local backup utility for public-shell SQLite experiment rows and
request audit JSONL metadata. It writes a manifest and copies only configured
local public-shell files that already exist. The manifest records per-file size
and SHA-256 for isolated restore integrity checks. It does not inspect request
bodies, response bodies, credentials, private-core internals, runtime internals,
or customer secrets. It is not restore testing, production backup policy,
tenant backup, disaster recovery, customer validation, or product launch.

Data Restore Drill v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/DATA_RESTORE_DRILL_V0_1.md` records an
isolated local restore-readability drill for public-shell backup artifacts. It
copies backup SQLite and request audit JSONL files into a drill directory and
checks readability plus manifest size/SHA-256 integrity. It does not restore
into live paths, restore credentials, restore private core, call external
services, test production restore, provide tenant restore, or claim production
readiness.

Tenant Request Boundary v0.1 boundary:
`phase_b_product/commercial_readiness/TENANT_BOUNDARY_V0_1.md` records an
optional `X-SAEE-Tenant-ID` request-envelope guard for controlled preview. It
requires `SAEE_REQUIRE_TENANT_ID=true` and allowlisted
`SAEE_ALLOWED_TENANT_IDS` when enabled. Tenant IDs must be key-safe
alphanumeric/dot/underscore/hyphen identifiers up to 64 characters. It is not
tenant-isolated storage, tenant billing isolation, production authorization,
production multi-tenancy, customer validation, or product launch.

Zenodo Publish-Ready boundary:
`zenodo_publish_ready/` is a minimal safe, definition-only Zenodo package published at DOI `10.5281/zenodo.21135472` with concept DOI `10.5281/zenodo.21135471` and record URL `https://zenodo.org/records/21135472`. It contains only observational science content and metadata. It does not include executable code, runtime description, algorithmic detail, system architecture, kernel logic, fitness/selection/mutation mechanisms, lineage internals, or private implementation. This DOI is a definition-only publication and is not a runtime release, GitHub release, paper acceptance, or implementation disclosure.

Theory Compression boundary:
SAEE Theory Compression reduces existing theory, empirical alignment, and GSP into three compressed laws, one unified equation, and REDS-MO as a candidate universality class. It does not claim universal evolution theory or externally validated physical law.

Academic Positioning boundary:
SAEE Academic Positioning maps SAEE into ALife, evolutionary computation, complex systems, and self-modifying/reflexive systems. It is documentation-only and does not claim external validation, universal theory, or benchmark superiority.

Submission Freeze boundary:
SAEE Submission Freeze records the local paper-facing state as submission-ready for packaging as the LCR-REDS Object. It is not a manuscript submission, acceptance, publication, release, DOI, package upload, or external validation claim.

Final Architecture boundary:
SAEE Final Architecture Spec records a three-layer non-contamination contract: Layer 1 LCR-REDS defines scientific truth, Layer 2 SAEE-MP coordinates interpretation, and Layer 3 runtime/experiment instantiates behavior. It does not unfreeze LCR-REDS, add runtime behavior, add laws, add experiments, or claim external validation.

Final Interpretation boundary:
SAEE Final Interpretation Package converts the frozen scientific object into paper-facing abstract, introduction, contribution, related-work, positioning, and conclusion surfaces. It does not modify SAEE, extend theory, run experiments, add laws, claim universality, claim external validation, or indicate manuscript submission/publication.

ALife Format boundary:
SAEE ALife Format Package projects the frozen object into a local ALife-style LaTeX skeleton. It is not an official template compliance claim, submission, acceptance, publication, DOI, external validation, new theory, new experiment, new law, runtime change, or benchmark-superiority claim.

ALife Hostile Review Repair boundary:
SAEE ALife Hostile Review Repair fixes venue-compliance and claim-safety defects in the paper-facing package only. It must not add theory, experiments, laws, kernels, runtime behavior, external validation, publication, DOI, or submission claims.

ALIFE 2026 Late-Breaking Abstract boundary:
SAEE ALIFE 2026 Late-Breaking Abstract Package compresses the frozen object into a two-page LBA proof surface for the currently open route. It was submitted in Linklings as `lb120` with portal status `Under Evaluation` on `07/02/26`. It is not a Full Paper package, official-template compliance claim, acceptance, publication, DOI, release, external validation, new theory, new experiment, new law, runtime change, GSP change, or benchmark-superiority claim.

Commercial Readiness State Consistency Audit boundary:
Current state is `status=pass_consistent_hold_state`, `commercial_status=hold`,
`external_calibration_status=completed_with_human_results_hold`,
`external_calibration_validation_status=hold`,
`external_validation_success_claim=false`, `internal_self_play_status=pass`,
`production_ready=false`, `customer_validated=false`, and
`product_launched=false`. This verifies status consistency only; it does not
authorize launch, customer validation, external validation success, blocker
closure, workbook import, or production-readiness claims.

Twenty-five runs completed the closed rehearsal contract. DeepSeek completed 10/10 with three observed Tool paths and mixed_within_study execution; Doubao completed 10/10 with one Tool path and consistent_within_study execution; GLM completed 5/10 with five contract failures, so its path metrics cover only the five contract-complete runs. Every contract-complete run detected TEST_FAILURE and APPROVAL_MISSING, and Evidence outcomes were identical within each Agent: AUTHORIZED_AGENT_ACTION and HUMAN_OVERSIGHT failed with approval_record and passing_test_result missing. study_complete=true means all 30 planned executions were recorded; it does not mean all runs succeeded. ranking_generated=false, leaderboard_generated=false, winner_selected=false, intelligence_score_generated=false, reliability_probability_estimated=false, external_world_actions=false, customer_data=false, and production_ready=false. ## SAEE Baidu entry authorization and live Qianfan update — 2026-07-13

The owner chose to withhold a public license and authorized local Git commits only; tag, push and GitHub Release remain unauthorized. Two bounded synthetic business scenarios completed real Baidu Qianfan function-calling roundtrips through the two-operation SAEE product adapter, totaling four Provider rounds. Sanitized receipts contain hashes and structured results but no credentials or raw Provider text. Both Provider summaries omitted required false boundaries, so the host used deterministic canonical-summary fallback. qianfan_real_provider_product_roundtrip=true, qianfan_live_synthetic_scenario_count=2, qianfan_live_provider_round_count=4, external_world_actions=0, official_qianfan_integration=false, customer_validated=false, marketplace_listed=false, and production_ready=false. Baidu contact and Qianfan partner application are authorized, but verified company/contact fields remain required.

The Qianfan partner consultation has a schema-backed Agent-readable application payload and fail-closed validator. Owner-provided company/contact fields and explicit contact consent were transmitted to the official Baidu form.
